title: If only
goal: Talk about what you would do if things were different, what you would have done, what you wish, what you regret, and your plans and hopes for life.
intro:
Late-night conversations with friends sooner or later turn to 'what if': if I were rich, if I'd studied harder, if I'd taken that chance, if I go abroad. Young Afghans and Pakistani Pashtuns talk a lot about the future — jobs, marriage, emigration — and about luck and fate.

In unit 19 you met **وای** (wāy) for things that aren't true. Now you'll use it yourself: **که زه شتمن وای** 'if I were rich', **ما به کړی وای** 'I would (have) done', **کاشکې** 'I wish', and the everyday ways to hope (**خدای دې وکړي!**) and to regret.

grammar.title: 'If I were …': که … وای
grammar.body:
In unit 19 you met **وای** (wāy), the 'unreal' form of 'to be'. It is used for things that are **not true now**: 'if I were rich', 'if you were here'. The good news: **وای never changes** — the same word for every person, singular and plural, masculine and feminine.

Both halves of the sentence use it:

که زه شتمن **وای** 'if I were rich' · که ته دلته **وای** 'if you were here'
… ښه **به وای** 'it would be nice' · … زه **به** په کابل کې **وای** 'I would be in Kabul'

So: **که** + … + **وای**، … + **به** + … + **وای**. In the result half, به comes in its usual second place, and وای goes at the end.

**Negative:** **نه وای**: که هوا يخه **نه وای** 'if it weren't cold', پرېشان به **نه وای** 'he wouldn't be worried'.

**Compare the real 'if'** (unit 19), for things that can still happen: که سبا وزګار **يم**، درځم 'if I'm free tomorrow, I'll come'. The moment you mean 'but I'm not', switch to وای: که نن وزګار **وای**، درتلای … 'if I were free today …'.

**The trap:** don't use وي (wi, the ordinary subjunctive 'be') here. که ته دلته **وي** means 'if you are here' (maybe you will be); که ته دلته **وای** means 'if you were here' (but you aren't).

grammar.title: 'I would (have) …': به + participle + وای
grammar.body:
With any other verb, the unreal form is the **past participle + وای** (the participle is the -ay / -e / -i form you met in 'have done', unit 16): **تللی وای** 'would have gone', **کړی وای** 'would have done'. It goes in **both** halves: که ته **راغلی وای**، موږ به خوشاله **شوي وای** 'if you had come, we would have been happy'.

Pashto uses this same pattern for 'would' and 'would have': که زه شتمن وای، يو کور **به مې اخيستی وای** is 'if I were rich, I'd buy a house' or 'I'd have bought a house'. The context tells you which one is meant.

**Agreement works as in the past tense:**
- **Intransitive** verbs (go, come, stay, become) agree with the **subject**: زه به **تللی** وای (man) · زه به **تللې** وای (woman) · موږ به **تللي** وای.
- **Transitive** verbs are **ergative**: the doer is ما / تا / هغه or a clitic (مې، دې، يې، مو), and the participle agrees with the **object**: سفر (m) به مې **کړی** وای · پيسې (f pl) به مې جمع **کړې** وای · ويزه (f) به مې **اخيستې** وای. For 'tell' with a چې-clause, use the masculine plural **ويلي**.

**Negative:** نه goes **before** وای, and the participle moves after it: زه به **نه وای** راغلی 'I wouldn't have come', ما به دا **نه وای** کړي.

**The trap:** after که, don't use the plain past (لاړم، وليد) for something that didn't happen. که لاړم means 'when I went'; که **تللی وای** means 'if I had gone'.

grammar.title: Wishes, hopes and regrets: کاشکې and خدای دې وکړي
grammar.body:
**کاشکې** (kā́shke) 'I wish, if only' starts the sentence, and what follows depends on whether the wish can still come true.

**1. Impossible now, or about the past → وای / participle + وای** (the two patterns above):
کاشکې زه هلته **وای** 'I wish I were there'
کاشکې ما ورته **ويلي وای** 'I wish I'd told him'

**2. A hope for the future → the subjunctive** (perfective present, as after چې):
کاشکې سبا هوا ښه **شي** 'I hope the weather's nice tomorrow'

For hopes, people even more often say **خدای دې وکړي** (lit. 'may God do it') — on its own as 'let's hope so!', or with چې + subjunctive: خدای دې وکړي چې ته بريالی **شې** 'I really hope you succeed'. **انشاالله** and **که خدای کول** 'God willing' go with plans: که خدای کول، بل کال به … .

**Regret:** **پښېمانه يم چې** + past 'I regret that …', **افسوس چې** + past 'it's a pity that …': افسوس چې درسره **رانغلم** 'shame I didn't come with you'.

**The trap:** کاشکې + the plain past is wrong for regrets: say کاشکې **تللی وای** 'I wish I'd gone', not کاشکې لاړم.

examples.roman: xudā́y de wə́kṛi che tə baryā́lay she.

culture:
Plans in Pashto almost always come wrapped in **انشاالله** or **که خدای کول** 'God willing' — not as a polite 'maybe', but because saying 'I will' flatly sounds presumptuous. Hopes are answered with **خدای دې وکړي!** or **انشاالله**, and things that didn't work out are put down to fate: **بخت مې نه و** or **قسمت نه و** 'it wasn't meant to be', which is also a kind way to console a friend.

For many young Pashtuns the big 'what if' is **مهاجرت**: going to Europe, the UK, North America, or for work to Dubai and the Gulf. Almost every family has someone abroad, and the conversation about leaving or staying — duty to parents, marriage, the longing for the **وطن** that runs through Pashto songs and *landay* — is one you'll hear again and again. Listen with sympathy and don't give strong advice unless you're asked; **ستا خيال څه دی؟** 'what do you reckon?' keeps the conversation open.

lessons.title: If I were rich …

tip.title: 'If I were …': که … وای
tip.body:
- **وای** is 'were / would be' for things that aren't true. It never changes.
- Both halves: **که** زه شتمن **وای**، خوشاله **به وای**.
- Not true → وای. Might happen → وي: که ته دلته **وي** 'if you're here'.

lessons.title: What I would have done

tip.title: 'would (have)': به + participle + وای
tip.body:
- Other verbs: participle + **وای**: تللی وای 'would have gone', کړی وای 'would have done'.
- Intransitive agrees with the subject (تللی / تللې); transitive is ergative and agrees with the object: پيسې به مې جمع **کړې** وای.
- Negative: به **نه وای** راغلی.
tip.pattern: که … participle + وای، … به + participle + وای

sentences.en: If you'd come a bit earlier, you'd have seen him.

sentences.native: ښه شوه چې ته راغلې، که نه زه به يوازې پاتې شوی وای.
sentences.roman: ṣə shwa che tə rā́ġle, ka na zə ba yawā́ze pā́te shə́way wāy.
sentences.en: Good thing you came, otherwise I'd have been left on my own.

sentences.native: دا ښه فرصت و، خو بخت مې ونه کړ.
sentences.roman: dā ṣə fursát wə, xo baxt me wə́na kaṛ.
sentences.en: It was a good chance, but luck wasn't on my side.

sentences.native: په کاروبار کې هر څوک بخت ته اړتيا لري.
sentences.roman: pə kārobā́r ke har tsok baxt ta aṛtiyā́ lári.
sentences.en: In business everybody needs luck.

sentences.native: هره مياشت لږ پيسې جمع کوم.
sentences.roman: hára miyā́sht ləẓ páyse jamʿ kawə́m.
sentences.en: I save a little money every month.

lessons.title: Wishes and regrets

tip.title: کاشکې — I wish
tip.body:
- Can't come true / past: **کاشکې** + وای or participle + وای: کاشکې زه هلته **وای**، کاشکې ما ويلي **وای**.
- A hope for the future: کاشکې + subjunctive, or **خدای دې وکړي چې** + subjunctive.
- Regret: **پښېمانه يم چې** + past.
tip.pattern: کاشکې + … وای · خدای دې وکړي چې + subjunctive

new: کاشکې ما ته دې مخکې ويلي وای.
هغه تېره خبره ده، هېره يې کړه.

sentences.native: کاشکې زه هم ستاسو سره وای!
sentences.roman: kā́shke zə ham stāso sara wāy!
sentences.en: I wish I were with you all!

sentences.native: کاشکې ما په ځوانۍ کې انګرېزي زده کړې وای.
sentences.roman: kā́shke mā pə dzwānə́y ke angrezí zdə kaṛé wāy.
sentences.en: I wish I'd learned English when I was young.

sentences.native: کاشکې پرون مې هغه ته زنګ وهلی وای.
sentences.roman: kā́shke parún me haġə́ ta zang wahə́lay wāy.
sentences.en: I wish I'd called him yesterday.

sentences.native: کاشکې بيا ځوان وای!
sentences.roman: kā́shke biyā́ dzwān wāy!
sentences.en: If only I were young again!

sentences.native: کاشکې سبا باران ونه شي.
sentences.roman: kā́shke sabā́ bārā́n wə́na shi.
sentences.en: I hope it doesn't rain tomorrow.

sentences.native: خدای دې وکړي چې ازموينه دې ښه تېره شي.
sentences.roman: xudā́y de wə́kṛi che azmóyəna de ṣa téra shi.
sentences.en: I hope your exam goes well.

sentences.native: پښېمانه يم چې ورته مې رښتيا ونه ويل.
sentences.roman: pṣemā́na yəm che wárta me rəṣtyā́ wə́na wayəl.
sentences.en: I regret not telling him the truth.

sentences.native: دا زما تېروتنه وه، بښنه غواړم.
sentences.roman: dā zmā terwatə́na wa, baṣə́na ġwā́ṛəm.
sentences.en: That was my mistake, I'm sorry.

sentences.native: هر څوک تېروتنه کوي.
sentences.roman: har tsok terwatə́na kawí.
sentences.en: Everyone makes mistakes.

sentences.native: ځواني مې په کار کې تېره شوه.
sentences.roman: dzwāní me pə kār ke téra shwa.
sentences.en: I spent my youth working. (lit. my youth passed in work)

lessons.title: Making a big decision

tip.title: 'It'd be better to …'
tip.body:
- **غوره به وي چې** + subjunctive: غوره به وي چې سبا پرېکړه **وکړو**.
- Asking for an opinion: **ستا خيال څه دی؟** 'what do you reckon?'; answering: **زما په خيال** …
- 'Go or stay?': لاړ شم **که** پاتې شم? — که is 'or' in questions.

new: په دې فکر کې يم چې…

sentences.native: غوره به وي چې سبا پرېکړه وکړو.
sentences.roman: ġwára ba wi che sabā́ prékṛa wə́kṛu.
sentences.en: It'd be better to decide tomorrow.

sentences.native: دا سخته پرېکړه ده.
sentences.roman: dā sáxta prékṛa da.
sentences.en: This is a hard decision.

sentences.native: ته ډاډه يې؟
sentences.roman: tə ḍā́ḍa ye?
sentences.en: Are you sure?

sentences.native: ستا خيال څه دی، لاړ شم که پاتې شم؟
sentences.roman: stā xayā́l tsə day, lāṛ shəm ka pā́te shəm?
sentences.en: What do you reckon — should I go or stay?

sentences.native: زما په خيال غوره به وي چې پاتې شې.
sentences.roman: zmā pə xayā́l ġwára ba wi che pā́te she.
sentences.en: I reckon it'd be better if you stayed.

sentences.native: په دې فکر کې يم چې دنده بدله کړم.
sentences.roman: pə de fikr ke yəm che dánda badála kṛəm.
sentences.en: I'm thinking of changing jobs.

sentences.native: دا ستا انتخاب دی، زه به درسره يم.
sentences.roman: dā stā intixā́b day, zə ba dərsara yəm.
sentences.en: It's your choice — I'll back you.

sentences.native: که زه ستا پر ځای وای، دا انتخاب به مې کړی وای.
sentences.roman: ka zə stā pər dzāy wāy, dā intixā́b ba me kaṛáy wāy.
sentences.en: If I were you, I'd make the same choice.

sentences.native: غوره دا ده چې له کورنۍ سره خبره وکړې.
sentences.roman: ġwára dā da che la kornə́y sara xabə́ra wə́kṛe.
sentences.en: Best to talk it over with your family.

sentences.native: نه، ډاډه نه يم، لږ وخت راکړه.
sentences.roman: na, ḍā́ḍa na yəm, ləẓ waxt rā́kṛa.
sentences.en: No, I'm not sure — give me a bit of time.

sentences.native: ستا په ژوند کې لوی هدف څه دی؟
sentences.roman: stā pə zhwand ke loy hadáf tsə day?
sentences.en: What's your big goal in life?

sentences.native: زما هدف دا دی چې خپل کاروبار ولرم.
sentences.roman: zmā hadáf dā day che xpəl kārobā́r wə́larəm.
sentences.en: My goal is to have my own business.

sentences.native: هيله لرم چې بريالی شې.
sentences.roman: híla lárəm che baryā́lay she.
sentences.en: I hope you succeed.

sentences.native: ته تکړه يې، خامخا به بريالی شې.
sentences.roman: tə takṛá ye, xāmaxā́ ba baryā́lay she.
sentences.en: You're capable — you'll definitely make it.

sentences.native: زه تمه لرم چې دا کال کار پيدا کړم.
sentences.roman: zə tamá lárəm che dā kāl kār paydā́ kṛəm.
sentences.en: I'm hoping to find work this year.

sentences.native: زه غواړم چې اولاد مې ښه زده کړه ولري.
sentences.roman: zə ġwā́ṛəm che awlā́d me ṣa zda kṛá wə́lari.
sentences.en: I want my children to get a good education.

sentences.native: زما په ژوند کې لوی بدلون راغلی دی.
sentences.roman: zmā pə zhwand ke loy badlún rāġə́lay day.
sentences.en: There's been a big change in my life.

sentences.native: فکر کول هېڅ ګټه نه لري، يو څه وکړه.
sentences.roman: fikr kawə́l hets gáṭa na lári, yaw tsə wə́kṛa.
sentences.en: Thinking won't help — do something.

sentences.native: که تکړه نه وای، دلته به نه وای.
sentences.roman: ka takṛá na wāy, dálta ba na wāy.
sentences.en: If you weren't good, you wouldn't be here.

lessons.title: Staying or going abroad
new: که خدای کول، بل کال به واده وکړم.

sentences.native: ډېر ځوانان د مهاجرت خوبونه ويني.
sentences.roman: ḍer dzwānā́n də muhājirát xobúna wíni.
sentences.en: Lots of young people dream of emigrating.

sentences.native: په پردي وطن کې ژوند اسان نه دی.
sentences.roman: pə pradí watán ke zhwand āsā́n na day.
sentences.en: Life in a foreign country isn't easy.

sentences.native: که ما مهاجرت نه وای کړی، اوس به له مور سره وای.
sentences.roman: ka mā muhājirát na wāy kaṛáy, os ba la mor sara wāy.
sentences.en: If I hadn't emigrated, I'd be with my mother now.

sentences.native: وطن مې ډېر ياد شوی دی.
sentences.roman: watán me ḍer yād shə́way day.
sentences.en: I really miss home.

sentences.native: که خدای کول، يوه ورځ به بېرته وطن ته راشم.
sentences.roman: ka xudā́y kawə́l, yáwa wradz ba bérta watán ta rā́shəm.
sentences.en: God willing, one day I'll come back home.

sentences.native: بهر ته تلل څه ګټه لري؟
sentences.roman: bahár ta tlə́l tsə gáṭa lári?
sentences.en: What's the point of going abroad?

sentences.native: خو که لاړ شې، له کورنۍ نه به لرې شې.
sentences.roman: xo ka lāṛ she, la kornə́y na ba lə́re she.
sentences.en: But if you go, you'll be far from your family.

sentences.native: که پردي وطن ته لاړ شم، پښتو به هېره نه کړم.
sentences.roman: ka pradí watán ta lāṛ shəm, paṣtó ba héra na kṛəm.
sentences.en: If I go abroad, I won't forget Pashto.

sentences.native: زما ورور پنځه کاله مخکې مهاجرت وکړ.
sentences.roman: zmā wror pindzə́ kā́la mə́xke muhājirát wə́kaṛ.
sentences.en: My brother emigrated five years ago.
